stage1.impression: A strong mood: a warm smoky pine wood with low backlight and long trunk shadows. But the trunks read as smooth beige CG columns: branchless, evenly lit and repeated. The smoke is a flat sepia wash with no shafts. The speaker is a near-black block: its tint, woofer and amplifier are lost, it has a rim on one edge only, and the horn looks dark and muddy.

blocking_9: The speaker reads as tinted acrylic, not a black void. The body's median luminance is 10 to 20, with a warm rim on both vertical edges and the horn's top, and the woofer outline shows through the tint.
Light shafts cut by the trunks are visible in the smoke: alternating bright and dark bands with at least 40 levels of contrast, instead of a uniform wash.
The trunks read as real pines: bark with deep plates, branch stubs, varied lean and taper, and the near trunks darker than the smoke behind them, not pale columns.
The brightest part of the smoke sits behind the speaker's silhouette, so the hero has the strongest figure-ground in the frame.
The grade is not a single sepia tone. Shadows and the shadowed ground carry some cool skylight, so the warm sun reads as warm.

defects.what: The woofer and front baffle are crushed to black (median 2.4, 66 % crushed); the tint and inner parts don't read.
The left edge of the cabinet has no rim light: a hard dark-to-background step with no warm edge, so the silhouette is lit on one side only.
The horn reads as a muddy dark-brown lump with a smeared interior. Its shape is hard to read.
The trunks are smooth cylinders with identical base flares, a uniform bright rim line on each and no branches. They read as plaster columns or a CG forest.
The near trunk is pale (median 102) and as light as the smoke around it, so the near-to-far depth layering is lost.
The smoke is a flat, featureless wash (range 38, and 21 in the upper right) with no shafts, no structure and no visible sun source.
The fallen trunk and roots at left read as a flat dark smear, half-sunk and pasted on.
The ground shadows are pure warm brown (r81 g54 b34). There is no skylight fill, so the whole frame is one sepia tone and looks graded, not photographed.
The tree shadows are parallel, evenly spaced bands that look procedural.
A trunk is clipped at the right frame edge and draws the eye to the border.

changes.problem: The hero is crushed to black: the tint, woofer and amplifier don't read, and there is a rim on the right edge only.

evidence.measured: lum_median 5.9, p95 34.5, crush_pct 32; woofer region [500,420,650,580] median 2.4, crush 66 %. Left edge step -86 with no rim; right edge rim step +120.

change.setting: Add a motivated fill: a large warm bounce (sunlit-litter colour, #C89A6A) 2 m in front of the speaker, camera-left, low at 0.5 m, plus a second sun-coloured rim kicker behind-left at azimuth -150°, elevation 10°
change.from: sun lamp only (azimuth 140°, irradiance 24); no fill, no left rim
change.to: a bounce area lamp 1.5 × 1.5 m at about 8 % of the sun's effect on the front, and a kicker irradiance 6 #FFB978 behind-left

changes.expected: The body lifts to median about 12 to 16. The woofer's surround and the amplifier box read through the tint. A thin warm rim appears on the left edge and the horn's top.

changes.problem: The idea of glowing smoke cut into shafts by the trunks doesn't read: the smoke is a uniform wash.

change.setting: Smoke: noise scale, cut, density; Sun lamp: angle
change.from: density 0.3, noise scale 1.4 m, cut 0.5, anisotropy 0.8, floor 0.006; sun angle 1.2°
change.to: density 0.18, noise scale 3.0 m, cut 0.6, anisotropy 0.85, floor 0.012; sun angle 0.5°. Add a sparse canopy (or a high branch gobo plane at 14 m) so the trunks and branches cast crisp shadow volumes through the smoke

changes.expected: Distinct diagonal bright and dark shafts in the smoke, with at least 40 levels of contrast between adjacent bands, and wisps with structure instead of a flat fog.

changes.problem: The modelled trunks read as smooth CG columns: no branches, identical flares, plastic-smooth bark.

evidence.measured: Seen at 2×: uniform surfaces, an identical bright rim line on every trunk, repeated base flare, no branch stubs.

change.from: 46 modelled cylinders, radius 0.15 to 0.27 m, pine_bark tinted 55 % toward #1E1A17, no canopy
change.to: scanned or procedurally varied pine trunks with branch stubs from 4 m up, ±2° random lean, ±20 % taper variation, bark displacement 2 to 3 cm, tint 75 % toward #1E1A17, and a sparse canopy above the frame

changes.expected: The trunks read as real Scots pine. The near trunks are dark and textured silhouettes against the smoke.

changes.problem: The brightest glow sits to the right of the frame, not behind the speaker. The speaker's head stands against mid-tones, so the figure-ground is weaker than the empty right side.

evidence.measured: behind the horn: lum_median 179. Right smoke [900,100,1150,300]: median 208. Profile at x 0 to 1200 rises left to right, 86 to 214.

change.setting: Sun lamp azimuth and elevation (and the smoke's centre to match)
change.from: azimuth 140°, elevation 12°; smoke centred 7 m behind
change.to: azimuth 170° (directly behind the speaker as the camera sees it), elevation 7°; shift the smoke's centre to sit on the camera-to-speaker axis

changes.expected: A bright glow peak centred behind the horn, with smoke behind the horn at median 200 or more and falling off towards both frame edges.

changes.problem: The whole frame is one sepia tone. The shadows carry no skylight, so it reads as a grade, not a morning.

evidence.measured: shadowed foreground: r81 g54 b34. Smoke: r223 g200 b180. Every region is warm.

changes.expected: The shadowed ground and the shadow sides of the trunks gain a slight neutral-to-cool fill, so the warm shafts separate from the shade.

changes.problem: The fallen trunk and roots at far left read as a flat, pasted dark smear and pull the eye to the edge.

evidence.measured: Seen: a flat dark shape, half-sunk, with no form lighting.

change.from: 5 pieces, one fallen trunk in the left foreground at mid-depth
change.to: remove the left fallen trunk; place 2 or 3 smaller roots and pine cones in the mid-ground, 1 to 3 m from the speaker, off the camera axis, partly in the sun shafts

changes.expected: A cleaner left edge, and texture at the speaker's depth that grounds it.

changes.problem: The horn and the top of the cabinet lose separation from each other and from the background mid-tones.

change.to: contrast 0.04, clarity 0.10, bloom 0.08 (keep the vignette at 0.15)

changes.expected: The horn's flare and interior shading read, and the rim stays crisp without a halo.

changes.problem: The speaker sits dead centre with symmetric empty space and no room for type. A trunk clipped at the right edge pulls the eye.

evidence.measured: Speaker centred at x 545 of 1200. A trunk is cut at the right frame edge.

change.to: azimuth -20°, 5.2 m, 65 mm, 0.8 m height, framed so the speaker sits on the left third; drop the edge trunk

changes.expected: The speaker sits on the left third, with the glowing smoke opening on the right as a clean field for type. The longer lens compresses the trunks into layered depth.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn read as attached, not floating on thin stalks above the cabinet.
out_of_scope.why: The mounting is the speaker's geometry. It is fixed.

out_of_scope.request: A lighter tint so the inner parts read more clearly.
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour is fixed (smoked black). Do it with light (c1), not a material change.
